Award the hit to Fencer Y with no penalty, because Fencer X's cross step was only a preparation, not an attack
Give Fencer X a yellow card and award no hit: the crossing step ended the phrase, so the remises are void
SAB-021.explain: Any forward movement in which the rear foot passes the front foot is forbidden at sabre: the referee halts the bout (t.23.5) and the offence is in the first group, a yellow card the first time (t.101.5; t.165; t.170 item 1.12). Fencer Y's stop-cut was the action made within the fencing time and it missed. Nothing started after the halt counts (t.23.3), so the remises are not counted at all. No hit is awarded, and the fencers are replaced where the bout was halted (t.22.7).

choices: Award the hit to Fencer X, since Fencer Y failed to find the blade (derobement)
Annul both hits as a simultaneous action, because both fencers started their attacks at the same time
Award the hit to Fencer Y, because Fencer Y was the one who attempted to deflect the opponent's blade first
Replace the fencers on guard, because the fault cannot be clearly assigned to either fencer
SAB-022.explain: If, when trying to find the opponent's blade to deflect it, the attacker does not find it (derobement), the right of attack passes to the opponent (t.102.2). The attacker who attempts to find the blade, fails, and continues is alone counted as hit (t.106.4.b). Fencer X gets the hit.

choices: Give a yellow card, but let the fencer fence with it; the glove only has to be replaced before the next bout
Red card straight away, because non-conforming equipment brought to the piste is a second group offence
Confiscate the glove with no penalty; the fencer has 5 minutes to get a conforming one
Confiscate the glove and give a yellow card (first group); the fencer has 5 minutes to get a conforming one
SAB-023.explain: The glove must have an elastic band, a popper button or another approved system to guarantee contact with the jacket sleeve (m.33.3). Non-regulation equipment on the piste is confiscated (t.70). Non-conforming clothing or equipment is a first group offence: a yellow card the first time, and the fencer must obtain regulation equipment in no more than 5 minutes (t.71; t.170 item 1.8).

choices: When the attacker touches the opponent's blade, even lightly, before starting the lunge
When the attacker first beats or takes the opponent's blade; mere contact is not enough
Always, because an attack takes precedence over a point in line
When the attacker straightens the arm before launching the lunge, as for any attack
SAB-024.explain: If the attack is initiated when the opponent has a point in line, the attacker must first deflect the opponent's blade, by a beat or by taking the blade. Referees must ensure that a mere contact of the blades is not considered sufficient (t.102.1). Without that, the attacker alone is counted as hit (t.106.4.a). Likewise the fencer in line who, after being beaten or taken, attacks or replaces the point in line instead of parrying is alone counted as hit (t.106.3.e).

choices: Only when the opponent's hit actually lands on the substituted area
Only after the fencer has already received a warning for the same fault earlier in the bout
Only when the judges confirm it; the referee cannot decide this alone
When it occurs during the fencing phrase, whether or not a hit lands there
SAB-025.explain: At sabre it is forbidden to protect the target area or substitute another part of the body for it by covering it. If this happens during the fencing phrase, any hit scored by the fencer at fault is annulled and the offence is in the first group, whether or not the opponent's hit lands there (t.97.2; t.30.1; t.170 item 1.4).

choices: Award the hit to Fencer X, because Fencer X made the parry and the renewed attack came too late
Annul both hits as a simultaneous action, because the lights came on together
Award the hit to Fencer Y: the delayed riposte gave Fencer Y the right to renew the attack
Replace the fencers on guard because the phrase cannot be judged with certainty
SAB-026.explain: The fencer who, after a successful parry, makes a momentary pause (delayed riposte) which gives the opponent the right to renew the attack is alone counted as hit (t.106.3.c). Only an immediate, simple riposte annuls the attacker's later actions (t.105.1).

choices: Annul both hits as a simultaneous action, because both fencers hit at the same time
Award the hit to Fencer X: the point in line came first and Fencer Y failed to find the blade (derobement)
Award the hit to Fencer Y, because an attack with a step-forward-lunge always has priority over a point in line
Award the hit to Fencer Y, because Fencer Y attempted to deflect the blade by stepping forward
SAB-027.explain: Fencer X had the point in line before Fencer Y started to attack, so Fencer Y had to deflect the blade first (t.102.1). Fencer Y tried to find the blade but failed (derobement), so the right of attack passes to Fencer X (t.102.2). The attacker who does this and continues is alone counted as hit (t.106.4.a-b). This assumes Fencer X keeps the line and hits with the tip of the blade.

choices: Award the hit to Fencer Y: the beat on the forte gives the right to an immediate riposte
Award the hit to Fencer X, because a beat on the blade always keeps the priority of the attack
Annul both hits as a simultaneous action, because both landed at the same time
Replace the fencers on guard, because it cannot be determined who was at fault
SAB-028.explain: A beat made on the forte (the third of the blade nearest the guard) means the attack is badly executed and gives the opponent the right to an immediate riposte. Only a beat on the foible (the two thirds furthest from the guard) keeps the attack's priority (t.104).

choices: Award the hit to Fencer Y, because a point in line established at the start of the bout always has priority
Replace the fencers on guard, because it cannot be determined whose action started first
Award the hit to Fencer X: the attack began first, so Fencer Y's point in line is only a counter attack
Annul both hits as a simultaneous action, because both fencers acted right after the command
SAB-029.explain: A point in line only obliges the attacker to deflect it when it was established before the attack began (t.102.1). The attack started first and was correct (t.101.3-4); Fencer Y, as the fencer attacked, who makes a stop hit is alone counted as hit (t.106.3.a).

choices: Award the hit to Fencer X, because a compound attack always has priority over any riposte
Award the hit to Fencer Y, who found the blade during a feint and riposted immediately
Annul both hits as a simultaneous action, because they landed at the same time
Replace the fencers on guard, because it cannot be determined who was at fault
SAB-030.explain: If, during a compound attack, the opponent finds the blade during one of the feints, the opponent has the right to riposte (t.103). The attacker who allows the opponent to find the blade and continues the attack while the opponent ripostes immediately is alone counted as hit (t.106.4.c).
